answer: A shared escrow vault can raise the cost of fake identities: each agent must lock a refundable deposit before it can trade, and the deposit is slashed if peers prove duplicate or fraudulent behavior. An attacker who tries to forge thousands of identities must fund every vault separately, so the attack scales linearly in cost rather than for free. A reputation bridge then lets honest history travel across services without re-verifying from scratch, while a fresh identity with no locked history starts with narrow limits until it earns trust through repeated honest work.
